Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Windsor Johnston.
The Supreme Court is preparing to hear arguments
over the Trump administration's use
of third country deportations next month.
NPR's Franco Ordonez reports.
Since taking office, President Trump has expanded
the controversial practice of deporting thousands of people
to countries where they have no ties.
Earlier this year, the Supreme Court said Trump
can temporarily resume the deportations,
which had been blocked by a lower court,
and scheduled oral arguments for next month.
Lawyers fighting the program argue
that many of these migrants are longtime residents
with no criminal history,
and that they face significant harm
being sent to third countries.
Some that have records of torture and persecution.
The case carries significant implications,
not only for Trump's immigration agenda,
but also for the broader scope of presidential power.
Franco Ordonez, NPR News.
China says it plans to retaliate
if the U.S. moves ahead with proposed new tariffs.
NPR's Jennifer Pack reports the warning comes
as the two countries negotiate a long-term trade agreement.
The U.S. wants to impose new tariffs
on the European Union and 13 countries, including China.
U.S. tariffs on Chinese exports could go up to 20%
or as high as 40%, and the Trump administration
says this is a response to excess capacity,
something China's foreign ministry rejects.
The so-called issue of overcapacity is a false proposition,
says spokesperson Guozia Kun,
using it as a pretext for political manipulation, he says.
President Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping
have had three friendly meetings this year,
but the underlying U.S.-China relationship remains tense.
Jennifer Pack, NPR News, Beijing.
Israeli airstrikes across Gaza have killed
at least 10 people today,
including a senior education official.
NPR's Anas Bamba reports on a growing campaign
targeting Gaza's civilian administration.
Palestinian health officials say 56-year-old Khalid Abu Nada,
Gaza's deputy minister of education and his wife,
were killed in an Israeli airstrike on their apartment.
Israel confirmed the strike,
saying Abu Nada oversaw Gaza's economy
and education portfolios.
Gaza's health ministry says around 300 school-aged children
have also been killed in Israeli attacks
during the ceasefire.
The deaths underscore the widening scope
of Israeli attacks during the ceasefire,
targeting not only militants,
but also police and civilian officials
responsible for keeping basic services running.
These attacks come as Israeli is blocking
a civilian intern committee of Palestinian officials
from entering Gaza to take over governance from Hamas.
Anas Bamba, NPR News, Gaza.
This is NPR News.
King tides and powerful surf have torn away
part of a pier just south of San Francisco.
A large wave knocked a section of it
into the ocean on Wednesday.
Some beachfront homes in Pacifica are flooding
as the highest tides of the year come in.
Farther north, officials in Marin County
have lifted an evacuation order
for residents in Stinson Beach.
The Pittsburgh Steelers have released quarterback
Aaron Rodgers after he publicly criticized
head coach Mike McCarthy.
Things escalated after he was benched
following Sunday's loss to the Philadelphia Eagles.
Jeremy Scott with member station WESA reports.
Less than a day after the Steelers
announced they were benching Rodgers,
the Super Bowl champion quarterback
criticized Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy
on ESPN's The Pat McAfee Show,
saying McCarthy fell asleep last week
in a team meeting and identified the Steelers
as the Green Bay Packers during a recent team huddle
when the Steelers were visiting the Philadelphia Eagles.
McCarthy did not offer many specifics
on the release of Rodgers, but said about his benching.
- It was a process that went on throughout this week
and we got to a point.
We talked about some communication and things like that
and there was an ultimatum made clearly
out of his job description.
So it was my decision to bench him.
- The team has named Mason Rudolph,
the starting quarterback moving forward.
For NPR News, I'm Jeremy Scott in Pittsburgh.

Stocks resume trading tomorrow.
